title: Unreliable Airspeed
ref: FCTM ch.8 Airspeed Unreliable (NG 8.29 / MAX 8.30) · QRH NNC 10.1 · PI-QRH Flight With Unreliable Airspeed
intro: A blocked pitot gives no warning. Airspeed lies; attitude and N1 tell the truth. Pitch and power first, checklist second.

chapters.title: When the airspeed lies
body: FCTM causes: pitot/static system, AOA vanes, ADIRU, radome damage.
Pitot ram inlet blocked only: pressure bleeds out through the drain holes and IAS slowly drops to zero.
Ram inlet AND drains blocked: trapped pressure, unpredictable IAS. It rises in a climb and falls in a descent: the ASI behaves like an altimeter.
Erroneous AOA corrupts airspeed and altitude on the side of the bad vane.
bullets: IAS DISAGREE / ALT DISAGREE / AOA DISAGREE
Continuous or intermittent stick shaker
Overspeed, AIRSPEED LOW, erroneous min/max speed bars
Speed/altitude not consistent with pitch and thrust
EEC ALTN light(s), radome damage or loss

quote.text: Early recognition of erroneous airspeed indications requires familiarity with the interrelationship between attitude, thrust setting, and airspeed. A delay in recognition could result in loss of airplane control.

chapters.title: Four items, right now
body: As soon as airspeed is suspect: disconnect everything that follows the bad speed, then set a known gear-up attitude and N1.
bullets: Autopilot (if engaged) . . . Disengage
Autothrottle (if engaged) . . . Disengage
F/D switches (both) . . . OFF
Set the following gear up pitch attitude and thrust: Flaps extended 10° and 80% N1 · Flaps up 4° and 75% N1

quote.text: Memory items for target pitch and thrust must be accomplished as soon as airspeed indications are suspected to be incorrect.

chapters.title: Why 10/80 and 4/75?
body: The settings work for all models and engines, at all weights and altitudes. The goal is to stay inside the envelope, not to hold level flight.
Flaps up: above stall, below overspeed. Flaps extended: above stall, below the flap placard.
bullets: Flaps extended → the airplane climbs
Flaps up → slight climb when light/low, slight descent when heavy/high
Deliberately biased toward high energy
Keep the current flaps until stabilized; any change → PI-QRH table

quote.text: The settings are biased toward a higher airspeed because a high-energy state is safer than being in a low-energy state.

chapters.title: What you can still trust
body: QRH item 6 lists the reliable indications. Stick shaker, overspeed and AIRSPEED LOW may sound erroneously or simultaneously. FPV and PLI may be unreliable.
One-side clues: stick shaker on one side, airspeed low on one side, PLI on one side. Suspect AOA: AOA DISAGREE plus wrong speed bars on one side → compare the PFDs with the ISFD.
Pitot/static cause: the AOA indicator (as installed), needle at about three o'clock ≈ safe maneuver/approach speed regardless of flaps.
bullets: Attitude
N1
Ground speed (FMC, ND, ATC radar)
Radio altitude

quote.text: Comparing only two corresponding airspeeds is not a conclusive indication to determine a reliable airspeed indication. The two corresponding airspeeds can still both be unreliable.

chapters.title: Trimmed, stabilized, then compare
body: No obvious reliable source? PF sets pitch and thrust from the Flight With Unreliable Airspeed table (phase, configuration, weight, altitude), trims, and waits.
Stabilized = thrust and pitch set, no further trim needed. It is not instantaneous.
Then compare captain, F/O and standby airspeeds with the table.
bullets: CLIMB (280/.76) · CRUISE (.76/280) · DESCENT (.76/280) · HOLDING (VREF40 + 70)
Phase/config change: thrust → pitch → configure → recheck → trim
Never change configuration before trimmed and stabilized

quote.text: An airspeed indication that differs by more than 20 knots or 0.03 Mach from the airspeed shown in the table should be considered unreliable.

chapters.title: Which side is good?
bullets: Captain's or F/O's reliable → Flight director switch (reliable side) ON; Autopilot (reliable side, if needed) Engage — may not engage or may disconnect
Do not use the autothrottle.
Only standby reliable → no autopilot, autothrottle or flight directors
None reliable → PI-QRH tables for the rest of the flight; check Non-Normal Configuration Landing Distance
Both CA and FO altitudes unreliable → not RVSM, transponder altitude reporting off; tell ATC
body: Flying on tables only: stay visual if possible, configure early, RA available below 2,500 ft, use electronic and visual glideslope.

quote.text: If the flight crew recognizes an unreliable airspeed condition and concludes that a reliable airspeed indication is not available, safe flight can still be conducted.

chapters.title: From takeoff to touchdown
bullets: Takeoff at/after V1: keep takeoff thrust, rotate toward 15° then normal takeoff pitch target, gear up, keep flaps, climb to acceleration height, then NNC
Descent: idle to 10,000 ft using pitch and V/S from the table; 2,000 ft above level-off → 1,000 fpm
Approach: ILS or GLS if available, landing configuration early, set table pitch/thrust at glideslope intercept, control descent rate with thrust
Landing: touch down 1,000–1,500 ft beyond the threshold, no float; autobrakes if available
Go-around: GA thrust, toward 15° then normal takeoff pitch; at a safe altitude, NNC pitch/thrust. Only standby reliable → Do not use TO/GA

quote.text: Fly the airplane on to the runway, do not hold it off or let it “float” to touchdown.

chapters.title: Same reflex, different details
body: Memory items, 10°/80% – 4°/75% and the 20 kt / 0.03 M criterion are identical on NG and MAX (QRH 10.1). FCTM text is identical.
MAX QRH adds a note: the Stick Shaker Indicator, digital readout, analog needle and approach reference band of the AOA indicator may be unreliable if the cause is erroneous AOA.
MAX: erroneous AOA can also trigger SPEED TRIM FAIL (AOA vane difference 5.5° or greater) — FCTM MAX 8.35.
bullets: NG transponder: ALT SOURCE selector (1 or 2) · TA ONLY · ALT RPTG OFF
MAX transponder: ALT selector (1 or 2) · TA · ALT OFF

qcm.q: Climbing with pitot ram inlet AND drain holes blocked. What does IAS do?
o: It oscillates around the true value
qcm.w: Trapped pressure makes the ASI act like an altimeter: IAS rises in a climb. A slow drop to zero is the inlet-only blockage with open drains.

qcm.q: Flaps up, airspeed suspect. Which pitch and thrust do you set?
qcm.w: QRH 10.1: Flaps up 4° and 75% N1; Flaps extended 10° and 80% N1.

qcm.q: Correct order of the Airspeed Unreliable memory items?
o: PROBE HEAT ON, AP, A/T, pitch/thrust
AP, A/T, F/D switches (both) OFF, pitch/thrust
qcm.w: Autopilot Disengage, Autothrottle Disengage, F/D switches (both) OFF, then gear-up pitch and thrust. PROBE HEAT is item 5, below the dashed line.

qcm.q: Which is NOT listed as reliable in QRH item 6?
qcm.w: Reliable: Attitude, N1, Ground speed, Radio altitude. The QRH notes the FPV and PLI may be unreliable.

qcm.q: On the PI table, trimmed and stabilized: when is an airspeed indicator unreliable?
o: Differs by more than 10 kt or 0.01 M
Differs by more than 15 kt or 0.05 M
Differs by more than 20 kt or 0.03 M
As soon as two indicators disagree
qcm.w: QRH 10.1 step 9: more than 20 knots or 0.03 Mach from the table airspeed.

qcm.q: Captain and F/O airspeeds agree. Conclusion?
o: Not conclusive: both can still be unreliable
Both are reliable, re-engage the A/T
The standby must be the failed one
qcm.w: FCTM: comparing only two airspeeds is not conclusive; both can be wrong (e.g. both pitots iced).

qcm.q: Only the standby airspeed is reliable. What does the QRH say?
o: Do not use the autopilot, autothrottle, or flight directors
qcm.w: QRH 10.1 step 11. For a go-around in this case: Do not use TO/GA.

qcm.q: Airspeed fails at V1+5 kt on takeoff. FCTM technique?
o: Keep takeoff thrust, rotate toward 15° then normal pitch, gear up, keep flaps
qcm.w: FCTM: maintain takeoff thrust, rotate towards 15°, retract gear, maintain flap configuration until acceleration height, then the NNC.

sources.quote: Flaps extended . . . . . . . . . . 10° and 80% N1 / Flaps up . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 4° and 75% N1
The following indications are reliable: Attitude N1 Ground speed Radio altitude
An airspeed indication that differs by more than 20 knots or 0.03 Mach from the airspeed shown in the table should be considered unreliable.
Note: The Stick Shaker Indicator on the Angle of Attack indicator may be unreliable.
If the ram air inlet to the pitot head is blocked, pressure in the probe is released through the drain holes and the airspeed slowly drops to zero.
The settings are biased toward a higher airspeed because a high-energy state is safer than being in a low-energy state.
SPEED TRIM FAIL light (Only and when difference between AOA vanes is 5.5° or greater)
maintain takeoff thrust, smoothly rotate towards 15° pitch attitude and establish the normal takeoff pitch attitude target, retract the landing gear, and maintain flap configuration.

title: Upset Prevention & Recovery
ref: FCTM 7.21–7.25 Upset Recovery · QRH MAN Upset Recovery (NG MAN.1.9 / MAX MAN.1.10)
intro: Nose high, nose low, wild bank: two scenarios, one logic. Recognize, disconnect, recover — and always unstall first.

chapters.title: What is an upset?
body: Historic definition: unintentionally exceeding any of these limits, or flying at an airspeed inappropriate for the conditions.
Current definition (AUPRTA): any time the airplane deviates from the intended state — pitch, roll or airspeed.

quote.text: The latest revision of AUPRTA concludes that an upset condition exists any time that an airplane is deviating from the intended airplane state.

chapters.title: Read the PFD, not your inner ear
body: Confirm by crosscheck: attitude, airspeed, altitude and trends.
The PFD is the primary reference: pitch scale and blue/brown color coding.
The bank pointer stays perpendicular to the horizon at any pitch: roll toward it, the shortest way.
bullets: Higher than normal control forces may be needed
Firm, continuous force on column and wheel
If a technique works, don't stack extra ones

quote.text: When completing the upset recovery maneuver, roll the shortest direction to wings level (toward the bank pointer).

chapters.title: Stalled? Unstall first
body: A stall can exist at any attitude. The QRH upset maneuvers assume the airplane is not stalled.
If stalled: apply and hold nose-down elevator until recovery is complete and the stick shaker stops. Some thrust reduction may be needed to stop the AOA increasing.
bullets: Stick shaker
Buffet, possibly heavy
Lack of pitch authority
Lack of roll control
Inability to stop a descent

quote.text: In all upset situations, it is necessary to recover from a stall before applying any other recovery actions.

chapters.title: Push, trim, reduce, roll
body: Speed decaying, trim nose up, and the instinct to add thrust: underwing engines pitch the nose up even more.
Trade altitude for airspeed. Up to full nose-down elevator, some nose-down trim — stop trimming as soon as g or elevator force lessens. Hold between 0 and 1 g.
bullets: Disengage autopilot. Disengage autothrottle.
Apply nose-down elevator. Apply as much elevator as needed to obtain a nose down pitch rate
Apply appropriate nose down stabilizer trim*
Reduce thrust
Roll (adjust bank angle) to obtain a nose down pitch rate.*
When approaching the horizon, roll to wings level · Check airspeed and adjust thrust · Establish pitch attitude.

quote.text: Pilots should not fly the airplane using stabilizer trim, and should stop trimming nose down when they feel the g force on the airplane lessen or the required elevator force lessen.

chapters.title: Roll first, pull later
body: Altitude turns into airspeed fast. Pulling at high bank only tightens the turn and loads the structure.
Do not increase g or use nose-up elevator/trim until approaching wings level. Speedbrakes as needed.
bullets: Disengage autopilot. Disengage autothrottle.
Recover from stall, if needed
Roll in the shortest direction to wings level. If bank angle is more than 90 degrees, unload and roll.*
Apply nose up elevator · Apply nose up trim, if needed* · Adjust thrust and drag, if needed.

nums.s: no level flight within load limits

quote.text: Applying nose-up elevator at bank angles above 60° causes no appreciable change in pitch attitude and may exceed normal structure load limits as well as the wing angle of attack for stall.

chapters.title: Trim and rudder: sparingly
body: Minimal pitch trim during the initial recovery.
Rudder only if roll control is ineffective and the airplane is not stalled — and only a small amount, in the direction of the desired roll.
bullets: QRH WARNING: Excessive use of pitch trim or rudder can aggravate an upset, result in loss of control, or result in high structural loads.
Low energy (nose high) = extra caution with rudder

quote.text: Too much rudder applied too quickly or held too long may result in loss of lateral and directional control or structural failure.

chapters.title: PM calls, PF recovers
bullets: PM: Call out attitude, airspeed and altitude throughout the recovery.
PM: Verify all needed actions have been done and call out any continued deviation.
No flight director guidance during the recovery
body: NG vs MAX: FCTM text and QRH maneuver are identical (QRH NG MAN.1.9, MAX MAN.1.10). Only the page layout differs.

qcm.q: Historic upset definition: which is correct?
qcm.w: FCTM/QRH: pitch greater than 25° nose up, 10° nose down, bank greater than 45°, or inappropriate airspeed.

qcm.q: Upset with stick shaker. What is the very first recovery action?
o: Recover from the stall: hold nose-down elevator until the shaker stops
qcm.w: FCTM: in all upset situations, recover from a stall before any other recovery action.

qcm.q: Nose high, speed decaying. Effect of a large thrust increase?
qcm.w: FCTM: a large thrust increase "causes an additional pitch up". The QRH says Reduce thrust.

qcm.q: Nose high recovery: when do you stop nose-down trim?
o: When g force or required elevator force lessens
qcm.w: FCTM: stop trimming nose down when you feel the g force or elevator force lessen. Don't fly the airplane with trim.

qcm.q: Nose high, elevator alone doesn't stop the pitch rate. What bank may be needed?
o: About 45°, up to a maximum of 60°
qcm.w: FCTM: bank angles of about 45°, up to a maximum of 60°, could be needed.

qcm.q: Nose low, 110° of bank. QRH sequence?
o: Pull first to stop the descent
Unload and roll to the nearest horizon, then nose-up elevator
qcm.w: QRH: If bank angle is more than 90 degrees, unload and roll. Nose-up elevator only to complete the recovery.

qcm.q: Above which bank angle can level flight NOT be maintained within AFM load factor limits?
qcm.w: FCTM 7.25: at bank angles greater than 67°, level flight cannot be maintained within AFM load factor limits.

qcm.q: When may rudder be used to help roll?
o: Only if roll control is ineffective and not stalled, with a small amount
qcm.w: QRH: careful use of rudder only if roll control is ineffective and the airplane is not stalled. Too much = loss of control or structural failure.

sources.quote: Pitch attitude greater than 25° nose up • Pitch attitude greater than 10° nose down • Bank angle greater than 45°
In all upset situations, it is necessary to recover from a stall before applying any other recovery actions.
Bank angles of about 45°, up to a maximum of 60°, could be needed.
At bank angles greater than 67°, level flight cannot be maintained within AFM load factor limits.
Roll in the shortest direction to wings level. If bank angle is more than 90 degrees, unload and roll.*
Careful use of rudder to aid roll control should be considered only if roll control is ineffective and the airplane is not stalled.

title: Approach to Stall or Stall Recovery
ref: FCTM 7.11–7.16 Approach to Stall or Stall · QRH MAN.1.1
intro: The stick shaker fires: you don't save altitude, you reduce angle of attack. And on the 737, thrust pitches the nose up — handle with care.

chapters.title: AOA first, altitude second
body: Approach to stall = controlled flight; stall = out of control but recoverable. The recovery maneuver is the same.
Accidents: altitude was available, but no positive recovery at the warning → full stall all the way to the ground.
Recover at the first warning: stick shaker or initial buffet. Near cruise altitude and Mach they may be simultaneous.

quote.text: For this reason, emphasis has shifted from a recovery with minimum loss of altitude to reducing the angle of attack below the wing stalling angle of attack to complete a positive and efficient recovery.

chapters.title: Any attitude, any airspeed
body: Nose high, nose low, high or low bank, in a turn (accelerated stall). It is not always intuitively obvious.
bullets: Stick shaker (artificial)
Buffet (natural), could be heavy
Lack of pitch authority
Lack of roll control
Inability to arrest descent rate

quote.text: Do all recoveries from approach to stall as if an actual stall has occurred.

chapters.title: Hold, disconnect, push
body: No flight director commands during the recovery: they are not designed for it.
bullets: Hold the control column firmly.
Disengage autopilot and autothrottle.
Smoothly apply nose down elevator to reduce the angle of attack until buffet or stick shaker stops.
Nose down stabilizer trim may be needed.* (NG) / can be needed.* (MAX)

quote.text: To initiate the recovery, the angle of attack must be reduced below the wing stalling angle of attack.

chapters.title: Underwing engines: thrust pitches up
body: Low speed + high thrust: elevator authority may not be enough to pitch the nose down.
Column forward (up to full forward) + some nose-down trim. Stop trimming when g or column force lessens: too much trim = loss of control or high structural loads.
Add thrust smoothly. At takeoff or go-around (thrust already high), a thrust reduction may be needed.

quote.text: This is because airplanes with underwing-mounted engines have a nose-up pitch moment relative to increased thrust.

chapters.title: Wings level, thrust, speedbrakes in
bullets: Roll in the shortest direction to wings level if needed.**
Advance thrust levers as needed.
Retract the speedbrakes.
Do not change gear or flap configuration, except — During liftoff, if flaps are up, call for flaps 1.
body: Before the wing is unstalled, ailerons and spoilers are ineffective. Keep nose-down pressure to unload the wing. Rudder is normally not needed.
Recovering from nose low: don't pull too hard, or you get a secondary stall or sustained shaker.

quote.text: Extending or retracting the flaps during the recovery at other times results in an increased altitude loss.

chapters.title: High: descend. Low: PM watches the ground
body: Above about 20,000 ft the airplane is thrust limited: trade altitude for airspeed. Expect a bigger altitude loss.
Near the ground: PM calls any trend toward terrain. After takeoff, adjust pitch to reduce AOA while avoiding the ground; flaps up → call Flaps 1.
Erroneous continuous stick shaker after liftoff, airspeed V2 or greater and positive V/S: continue climbout to acceleration height, monitoring altitude and airspeed.

chapters.title: Stabilize, then rejoin the path
bullets: Check airspeed and adjust thrust as needed.
Establish pitch attitude.
Return to the desired flight path.
Re-engage the autopilot and autothrottle if desired.
PM: Monitor altitude and airspeed · call out any omissions · call out any trend toward terrain contact · Set the FLAP lever as directed.
body: Speedbrakes up: higher AOA for a given speed → earlier buffet and shaker, little effect on actual stall speed.
NG vs MAX: FCTM identical; QRH identical except wording ("may be needed" NG / "can be needed" MAX).

quote.text: WARNING: ** Excessive use of pitch trim or rudder can aggravate the condition, or can result in loss of control or in high structural loads.

qcm.q: When do you start the recovery?
o: Only once the stall is confirmed
At the first indication: stick shaker or initial buffet
qcm.w: FCTM/QRH: immediately at the first indication of stall (buffet or stick shaker).

qcm.q: Primary goal of the recovery per the current FCTM?
o: Reduce AOA below the wing stalling AOA
qcm.w: Emphasis has shifted from minimum altitude loss to reducing the angle of attack.

qcm.q: Why advance the thrust levers smoothly on a 737?
o: Underwing engines create a nose-up pitch moment
qcm.w: FCTM 7.12: underwing-mounted engines cause a nose-up pitch moment when thrust is increased.

qcm.q: Approach to stall during a go-around, thrust already high, pitch still increasing. FCTM option?
o: A thrust reduction may be needed
qcm.w: FCTM: during takeoff or go-around, a reduction of thrust can be needed to stop the AOA increasing.

qcm.q: Stick shaker at liftoff, flaps inadvertently up. What does the PF call?
qcm.w: QRH: Do not change gear or flap configuration, except during liftoff, if flaps are up, call for flaps 1.

qcm.q: Can you follow the F/D during the recovery?
o: Yes, if the A/P is off
No, do not use flight director commands
qcm.w: QRH Note: Do not use flight director commands during the recovery.

qcm.q: Continuous stick shaker after liftoff, airspeed at or above V2, positive V/S. FCTM guidance?
o: Continue climbout to acceleration height, monitoring altitude and airspeed
qcm.w: FCTM: some failures cause an erroneous shaker; if V2 or greater and V/S positive, continue to acceleration height.

qcm.q: Effect of extended speedbrakes on an approach to stall?
o: Higher buffet and shaker speeds, little effect on actual stall speed
qcm.w: FCTM 7.14: speedbrakes up → higher AOA for a given speed. The QRH says Retract the speedbrakes.

sources.loc: MAN.1.1 Approach to Stall or Stall Recovery
sources.quote: Smoothly apply nose down elevator to reduce the angle of attack until buffet or stick shaker stops.
During liftoff, if flaps are up, call for flaps 1.
emphasis has shifted from a recovery with minimum loss of altitude to reducing the angle of attack below the wing stalling angle of attack
Advance thrust levers smoothly because underwing-mounted engines cause a nose-up pitch moment when thrust is increased.
If an erroneous stick shaker is activated continuously and airspeed is V2 or greater and vertical speed is positive, continue climbout to acceleration height

title: Windshear
ref: FCTM 7.25–7.26 Windshear · FCOM SP.16.26–28 Adverse Weather · QRH MAN Windshear (NG MAN.1.13 / MAX MAN.1.14) · SOP §3.2
intro: Near the ground you may get 5 seconds. The best escape maneuver is the one you never fly: avoid, prepare, then TO/GA without hesitation.

chapters.title: Little time, little altitude
body: Below 500 ft the wind is mostly horizontal. An airspeed gain can be the precursor of an airspeed loss.
The trap: speed drops, the airplane pitches down to regain trim speed. If the pilot lowers the nose too → high sink rate.
At low altitude: trade airspeed for altitude. More pitch + maximum thrust = the airplane's full performance.

quote.text: As little as 5 seconds may be available to recognize and react to a degrading vertical flight path.

chapters.title: Look for the clues
bullets: Thunderstorm activity
Virga (rain that evaporates before reaching the ground)
Pilot reports
LLWAS warnings
body: Stay clear of cells, heavy precipitation and known windshear. Confirmed windshear: delay takeoff or do not continue the approach.
Predictive Windshear (PWS): automatic below 1,800 ft AGL, alerts at 1,200 ft AGL and below, 10 to 60 s warning. It will not detect everything (e.g. very dry events).

quote.text: If the presence of windshear is confirmed, delay takeoff or do not continue an approach.

chapters.title: Takeoff: buy margin
bullets: Full rated takeoff thrust, unless a fixed derate is required for dispatch performance
Flaps 5, 10 or 15 unless limited by obstacles/climb gradient
Longest suitable runway clear of known windshear
Consider increased VR up to the performance-limited weight VR, not above actual weight VR + 20 kt; shear at or after actual VR → rotate without hesitation
Know the initial climb pitch; stick shaker → reduce pitch; do not exceed the PLI

chapters.title: Approach: stable early
bullets: Flaps 30 for landing
Stabilized no lower than 1,000 ft above the airport
A/T off (or planned off): add a gust-type correction, max 15 kt
No large thrust or trim reductions on a sudden speed increase
A/P + A/T: more monitoring and recognition time

chapters.title: Alerts and unacceptable deviations
bullets: Predictive caution: "MONITOR RADAR DISPLAY" → maneuver to avoid
Takeoff roll: "WINDSHEAR AHEAD, WINDSHEAR AHEAD" → before V1 reject, after V1 escape
Approach: "GO–AROUND, WINDSHEAR AHEAD" → escape, or normal go-around at pilot's discretion
Reactive: two-tone siren + "WINDSHEAR, WINDSHEAR, WINDSHEAR" → escape
body: Below 1,000 ft AGL, uncontrolled changes in excess of:

chapters.title: TO/GA, max thrust, 15°
bullets: Disengage autopilot.
Push either TO/GA switch.
Aggressively apply maximum thrust*
Disengage autothrottle.
Simultaneously roll wings level and rotate toward an initial pitch attitude of 15°.
Retract speedbrakes.
Follow flight director TO/GA guidance (if available)**
body: * Maximum thrust: thrust levers full forward if EECs are in normal mode; terrain contact imminent → full forward. ** Do not exceed the Pitch Limit Indication.

quote.text: In all cases, the pitch attitude that results in intermittent stick shaker or initial buffet is the upper pitch attitude limit.
quote.src: QRH NG & MAX MAN Windshear Escape

chapters.title: Automation: yes, but watched
bullets: Push either TO/GA switch*** · Verify TO/GA mode annunciation. · Verify GA thrust. · Retract speedbrakes. · Monitor system performance****
Do not change flap or gear configuration until windshear is no longer a factor.
Maintain wings level to maximize climb gradient, unless a turn is required for obstacle clearance
Do not attempt to regain lost airspeed until windshear is no longer a factor.
body: In TO/GA the F/D holds target speed until V/S drops to about +600 fpm, then commands 15°, then intermittent shaker (SOP §3.2.7). Protection only with pitch in TOGA.
On an ILS, A/P and F/D hold the glideslope regardless of AOA or shaker: without TO/GA or manual takeover, the airplane can stall (SOP §3.2.8).

quote.text: WARNING: **** Severe windshear can exceed the performance of the AFDS. Be prepared to disengage the autopilot and autothrottle and fly manually.
quote.src: QRH NG & MAX MAN Windshear Escape

chapters.title: Windshear on the runway
body: Before V1: there may not be enough runway to stop. At VR, rotate at a normal rate toward 15°, then fly the escape once airborne.
Near VR with a sudden speed loss and not enough runway to stop: start a normal rotation at least 2,000 ft before the end of the runway, even if speed is low. Ensure maximum thrust.
NG vs MAX: maneuver, FCOM precautions and FCTM text are identical.

qcm.q: Initial pitch for the manual Windshear Escape Maneuver?
qcm.w: QRH: rotate toward an initial pitch attitude of 15°. 20° is the GPWS pull-up.

qcm.q: During the escape, airspeed keeps dropping. What do you do?
o: Lower the nose to regain it
Do not try to regain airspeed while windshear is a factor
qcm.w: QRH: Do not attempt to regain lost airspeed until windshear is no longer a factor; no configuration change.

qcm.q: Upper pitch limit during the escape?
o: The attitude giving intermittent stick shaker or initial buffet
The F/D, even beyond the PLI
qcm.w: QRH Note: intermittent stick shaker or initial buffet is the upper pitch limit; do not exceed the PLI.

qcm.q: "WINDSHEAR AHEAD, WINDSHEAR AHEAD" at 100 kt, before V1. Action?
o: Continue and fly the escape once airborne
qcm.w: QRH: predictive warning during takeoff roll — before V1 reject; after V1 Windshear Escape Maneuver.

qcm.q: On approach: "GO-AROUND, WINDSHEAR AHEAD". QRH options?
o: Escape maneuver, or a normal go-around at pilot's discretion
qcm.w: QRH: perform the Windshear Escape Maneuver, or, at pilot's discretion, perform a normal go-around.

qcm.q: Which uncontrolled deviation below 1,000 ft AGL indicates windshear?
qcm.w: QRH: 15 kt IAS, 500 fpm V/S, 5° pitch, 1 dot glideslope, unusual thrust lever position for a significant time.

qcm.q: Windshear suspected for takeoff: increased VR is limited to?
qcm.w: FCOM SP: performance-limited VR, not to exceed actual gross weight Vr + 20 knots. Shear at actual VR: rotate without hesitation.

qcm.q: Windshear on an ILS with the A/P engaged and no pilot action. Risk?
o: None, the A/P protects against stall
The A/P goes to TO/GA by itself
The A/P holds the glideslope regardless of AOA: speed below shaker, even a stall
qcm.w: SOP §3.2.8: A/P and F/D hold altitude/glideslope without regard to AOA; push TO/GA or fly manually.

sources.quote: As little as 5 seconds may be available to recognize and react to a degrading vertical flight path.
Simultaneously roll wings level and rotate toward an initial pitch attitude of 15 °.

Unacceptable flight path deviations are recognized as uncontrolled changes from normal steady state flight conditions below 1000 feet AGL, in excess of any of the following: 15 knots indicated airspeed, 500 fpm vertical speed, 5° pitch attitude, 1 dot displacement from the glideslope
not to exceed actual gross weight Vr + 20 knots
add an appropriate airspeed correction (correction applied in the same manner as gust), up to a maximum of 15 knots
Windshear detection mode operates automatically below 1800 ft. Above Ground Level (AGL), with alerts available at 1200 ft. AGL and below.
both the F/D and A/P attempt to hold the airplane on altitude, or on glideslope after glideslope capture, without regard to angle of attack or stick shaker limitations.

title: Engine Failure at or after V1
ref: FCTM 3.37–3.44 Takeoff – Engine Failure · SOP §4.1–4.2 · QRH Engine Failure or Shutdown (NG 7.16 / MAX 7.18)
intro: An engine quits after V1: you go. Rudder, a slower rotation, V2 to V2+20, nothing before 400 ft. The rest happens at acceleration height.

chapters.title: Yaw like a crosswind
body: Noise, vibration, possibly rapid yaw. One-engine controllability is excellent on the runway and in the air: VMCA is below VR and VREF.
Heading is the best indicator of correct rudder. Stop the yaw with rudder, not the wheel: wheel displacement raises spoilers.

quote.text: The airplane heading is the best indicator of the correct rudder pedal input. To counter the thrust asymmetry due to an engine failure, stop the yaw with rudder.

chapters.title: Slower, slightly lower
body: Between V1 and liftoff: smooth rudder, proportional to thrust decay.
Rotate at VR, smoothly and continuously, ½°/s slower than all-engine, to a pitch 2–3° below normal. Liftoff in about 5 s, then hold V2 to V2+20.
In flight, correct rudder roughly centers the control wheel (minimum drag).

quote.text: With an engine inoperative, a smooth continuous rotation is also initiated at VR; however, the target pitch attitude is approximately 2° to 3° below the normal all engine pitch attitude resulting in a 12° to 13° target pitch attitude.

chapters.title: V2 to V2 + 20
bullets: Minimum V2 and a positive climb; F/D commands V2 or existing speed up to V2 + 20
Failure between V2 and V2 + 20 → climb at the speed of the failure
Failure above V2 + 20 → pitch up to V2 + 20 and hold it to acceleration height
Positive rate on the altimeter → GEAR UP
No F/D: attitude and IAS are the pitch references

chapters.title: Nothing urgent below 400 ft
body: Fire or engine breakup: memory items once the flight path is under control, gear up and a safe altitude reached — minimum 400 ft AGL.
Simple failure: Engine Failure or Shutdown NNC after flap retraction, when conditions permit.
Immediate turn (EO procedure): normally not below 400 ft AGL, V2 to V2 + 20 with takeoff flaps. Bank 15° max until V2 + 15, then up to 30°.
A/P: above 400 ft AGL, with correct rudder or rudder trim.
bullets: Air Algérie SOP above 400 ft: "SET FIFTEEN DEGREES BANK ANGLE", then "STATE THE MALFUNCTION"

chapters.title: Acceleration height: level off, speed, flaps
body: FCTM: minimum flap retraction height with an engine inoperative is 400 ft AGL; Boeing training uses 1,000 ft AFE. Based on reaching flaps-up speed and MCT within 5 min (10 min optional).
Air Algérie SOP: MFRA is published by the takeoff performance calculation, minimum 800 ft HAA, 10-minute basis. Brief an all-engine AND an engine-out acceleration height for every takeoff.
At acceleration height: flaps-up speed on the MCP (or VNAV), F/D commands a near-level segment (0–200 fpm), retract flaps on schedule. No F/D: lower pitch for about level flight.

quote.text: As the airplane accelerates and flaps are retracted, adjust the rudder pedal position to maintain the control wheel centered and trim to relieve rudder pedal pressure.

chapters.title: CON, checklists, then decide
bullets: Flaps up and at/above flaps-up maneuver speed: LVL CHG (or VNAV), CON, climb to obstacle clearance altitude
Engine Failure or Shutdown checklist, then After Takeoff checklist, once flaps are up and thrust is set
Stay at flaps-up maneuver speed until clear of obstacles, then the engine-out schedule (CDU CLB)
Autothrottle disconnected before level-off
Noise abatement no longer required
body: SOP: "SET LEVEL CHANGE, MAX CONTINUOUS THRUST AND BANK ANGLE TWENTY FIVE", engage A/P, PF takes the radio and calls "ENGINE FAILURE OR SHUTDOWN CHECK-LIST".

chapters.title: ATM or derate: touch the levers?
bullets: ATM (assumed temperature): not required, but you may advance to full rated thrust — VMCG/VMCA are based on full rated thrust
Fixed derate: do NOT exceed the derate limit unless (FCTM) the captain judges terrain clearance cannot be assured / (SOP) terrain contact is imminent — loss of directional control possible
Combined ATM + derate: at most up to the derate limit

quote.text: This is because the takeoff speeds consider VMCG and VMCA only at the fixed derate level of thrust.

chapters.title: Same technique, different FMC and tail
body: Technique identical in both FCTMs.
NG: logic depends on FMC U10.7 and earlier (A/P delayed until flaps up + LVL CHG) or U10.8 and later (VNAV). MAX: VNAV logic, ENG OUT CLB page.
QRH: Engine Failure or Shutdown p.7.16 (NG) / 7.18 (MAX); ENGINE FIRE or Engine Severe Damage or Separation p.8.10 (NG) / 8.2 (MAX).

qcm.q: Best indicator of correct rudder input after an engine failure at V1?
qcm.w: FCTM 3.37: the airplane heading is the best indicator of the correct rudder pedal input.

qcm.q: Target rotation pitch with an engine inoperative?
qcm.w: FCTM: 2–3° below the normal all-engine pitch, giving 12° to 13°.

qcm.q: Rotation rate with an engine inoperative?
qcm.w: FCTM: 1/2° per second less than normal, approx 1.5° to 2.5° per second.

qcm.q: Engine fails at V2 + 30 kt in the initial climb. Speed to fly?
o: Pitch up to V2 + 20 and hold it to acceleration height
qcm.w: FCTM/SOP: above V2 + 20, increase pitch to reduce to V2 + 20 and maintain until acceleration height.

qcm.q: Engine fire on takeoff: when do you do the memory items?
o: Flight path under control, gear up, minimum 400 ft AGL
Immediately, even on the runway after V1
qcm.w: FCTM/SOP: once the flight path is under control, the gear is retracted and a safe altitude (minimum 400 ft AGL) is reached.

qcm.q: Immediate engine-out turn with takeoff flaps: bank limit?
qcm.w: FCTM/SOP: limit bank to 15° until V2 + 15 knots; up to 30° permitted at V2 + 15 with takeoff flaps.

qcm.q: Per the Air Algérie SOP, the engine-out MFRA is:
o: From the takeoff performance calculation, minimum 800 ft HAA
qcm.w: SOP §4.2.3. The FCTM gives 400 ft AGL as the Boeing minimum; 3,000 ft HAA is the NADP 1 acceleration height.

qcm.q: Fixed derate takeoff, engine fails. Advance the live engine's thrust lever?
o: No, unless terrain clearance can't be assured / contact is imminent: loss of directional control risk
qcm.w: FCTM 3.44: VMCG and VMCA are based only on the derate thrust. With ATM, by contrast, you may go to full rated thrust.

sources.loc: 3.37 Rotation and Liftoff – One Engine Inoperative
sources.quote: resulting in a 12° to 13° target pitch attitude. The rate of rotation with an engine inoperative is also slightly slower (1/2° per second less) than that for a normal takeoff, resulting in a rotation rate of approx 1.5° to 2.5° per second.
Accomplish the appropriate memory checklist items once the flight path is under control, the gear is retracted, and a safe altitude has been attained (minimum 400 feet AGL).
The minimum altitude for flap retraction with an engine inoperative is 400 feet AGL.
Limit bank angle to 15° until V2 + 15 knots. Bank angles up to 30° are permitted at V2 + 15 knots with takeoff flaps.
The minimum altitude for flap retraction with an engine inoperative is published through the takeoff performance calculation (minimum 800 ft HAA).

sources.loc: §4.2.7 Engine flame out on Takeoff procedure
sources.quote: SET LEVEL CHANGE, MAX CONTINUOUS THRUST AND BANK ANGLE TWENTY FIVE
a thrust increase following an engine failure could result in loss of directional control and should not be accomplished unless, in the opinion of the captain, terrain clearance cannot be assured.

title: Loss of Thrust on Both Engines
titleFr: Masterclass · Loss of Thrust on Both Engines
ref: FCTM 8.17–8.18 Loss of Thrust on Both Engines · QRH NNC 7.6 (NG & MAX)
intro: Sudden silence, two ENG FAIL alerts. Every second costs N2: memory items now, windmill speed, APU in parallel.

chapters.title: Use the N2 while it's high
body: Prompt action regardless of altitude or airspeed. The sooner the restart attempt, the better the windmill odds, thanks to the still-high RPM.
The in-flight start envelope shows where windmill starts were demonstrated in certification — not the only area where one can succeed.
bullets: QRH condition: both engines have a loss of thrust AND both ENG FAIL alerts show
Objective: restart at least one engine

quote.text: There is a higher probability that a windmill start will succeed if the restart attempt is made as soon as possible (or immediately after recognizing an engine failure) to take advantage of high engine RPM.

chapters.title: FLT, CUTOFF, IDLE
bullets: ENGINE START switches (both) . . . FLT
Engine start levers (both) . . . CUTOFF
When EGT decreases: Engine start levers (both) . . . IDLE detent
If EGT reaches a redline or there is no increase in EGT within 30 seconds: Engine start lever (affected engine) . . . Confirm . . . CUTOFF, then IDLE detent — repeat as needed
body: Identical on NG and MAX (QRH 7.6).

chapters.title: 275 or 300 kt
body: First reference item: the speed that keeps the windmill going.
Below 30,000 ft, speed above the crossbleed start envelope improves restart odds. Higher up, you may need to descend.

quote.text: Loss of thrust at higher altitudes may require descent to a lower altitude to improve windmill starting capability.

chapters.title: Memory items first, then APU — don't wait
bullets: Do not wait for a successful engine start before starting the APU.
APU . . . START
When APU is running: APU GEN switches (both) . . . ON, one at a time
body: Memory items come before the APU start (high N2). If the windmill fails, the APU provides electrics and air for a starter-assisted start.
Trap: APU GEN power on the buses is not an engine generator at idle. Don't advance the thrust lever too early.

quote.text: Initiate the memory portion of the LOSS OF THRUST ON BOTH ENGINES NNC before attempting an APU start for the reasons identified above.

chapters.title: Windmill or starter assist?
body: Neither engine starts: the QRH looks at N2.
N2 at or above the threshold → windmill start. Below → APU bleed available? starter assist; if not, windmill anyway.
bullets: Windmill: Thrust levers (both) Close · start lever CUTOFF, then IDLE detent
MAX only: ENG HYD PUMP (selected engine) OFF before the windmill start
Starter assist: Thrust levers Close · WING ANTI-ICE OFF · PACK switches (both) OFF · APU BLEED ON · Ignition BOTH · start lever CUTOFF · ENGINE START GRD · N2 at or above 11% → IDLE detent

chapters.title: Slow is not failed
body: Acceleration to idle can be very slow, especially at high altitude or in heavy precipitation. N2 steadily increasing + EGT within limits = do not interrupt.
Hung or stalled start: stagnant RPM and rising EGT. Limit: the lower of EGT redline and EGT start limit redline.
bullets: Engine stabilized: ENGINE START (operating engine) As needed · Thrust lever Advance slowly · Engine GEN ON
After starter assist: APU BLEED OFF, PACK (operating engine side) AUTO
MAX: ENG HYD PUMP (operating engine) ON and YAW DAMPER ON

quote.text: If N2 is steadily increasing and EGT stays within limits, do not interrupt the start.

chapters.title: Attitude, then the second engine
bullets: Both primary attitude displays failed → IRS MODE selectors (both) ATT — irreversible; about 30 s straight and level, constant speed; enter heading; no autopilot
Only F/O attitude failed → IRS TRANSFER BOTH ON L, no autopilot
One engine stays failed → Engine In-Flight Start checklist (NG p.7.24 / MAX p.7.26)
MAX, no APU GEN: advise cabin crew, CAB/UTIL OFF and IFE/PASS SEAT OFF
body: NG vs MAX: same memory items and speeds. Differences: windmill N2 threshold (11% NG / 8.5% MAX), ENG HYD PUMP and YAW DAMPER steps on MAX, cabin load shed on MAX.

qcm.q: First memory item of Loss of Thrust on Both Engines?
qcm.w: QRH 7.6: 1 ENGINE START switches (both) FLT; 2 Engine start levers (both) CUTOFF; 3 When EGT decreases, IDLE detent.

qcm.q: When do the start levers go back to IDLE detent?
qcm.w: QRH: When EGT decreases: Engine start levers (both) IDLE detent.

qcm.q: No EGT rise after selecting IDLE. How long before recycling the start lever?
qcm.w: QRH: EGT redline or no increase in EGT within 30 seconds → CUTOFF, then IDLE detent, repeat as needed.

qcm.q: Airspeed to set at FL350?
qcm.w: QRH: at or above FL270, 275 knots; below FL270, 300 knots.

qcm.q: When do you start the APU?
o: Only if the windmill start failed
Without waiting for a successful restart, after the memory items
qcm.w: QRH: Do not wait for a successful engine start before starting the APU. FCTM: memory portion first, to use the high N2.

qcm.q: 737 MAX, neither engine starts. N2 threshold for a windmill start?
qcm.w: QRH MAX: N2 is at or above 8.5% → windmill. On the NG the threshold is 11%.

qcm.q: During restart, N2 rises very slowly, EGT within limits. Action?
qcm.w: QRH: If N2 is steadily increasing and EGT stays within limits, do not interrupt the start.

qcm.q: Starter-assisted start: when does the start lever go to IDLE detent?
o: As soon as ENGINE START is in GRD
When N2 is at or above 11%
qcm.w: QRH (NG & MAX): When N2 is at or above 11%: Engine start lever IDLE detent.

sources.loc: NNC 7.6 Loss Of Thrust On Both Engines
sources.quote: 1 ENGINE START switches (both) . . . . . . . . . . FLT 2 Engine start levers (both) . . . . . . . . . . . CUTOFF 3 When EGT decreases: Engine start levers (both) . . . . . . IDLE detent
At or above FL270, set airspeed to 275 knots. Below FL270, set airspeed to 300 knots.
N2 is at or above 11%: Attempt a windmill start.
N2 is at or above 8.5%: Attempt a windmill start. ... 15 ENG HYD PUMP (selected engine) . . . . . . . . . OFF
CAB/UTIL switch . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . OFF IFE/PASS SEAT switch . . . . . . . . . . . OFF

sources.loc: 8.17 Loss of Thrust on Both Engines
sources.quote: Initiate the memory portion of the LOSS OF THRUST ON BOTH ENGINES NNC before attempting an APU start
do not confuse the establishment of APU generator power with the establishment of engine generator power at idle RPM, and avoid advancing the thrust lever prematurely.
